## [open] /mine copper_ore auto-pathed into mine_stair zone edge, dug into a self-made unescapable pocket — Thak, 2026-09-01
Not a wedge — real diagnostic caught the difference this time. `/mine copper_ore` picked its
nearest candidate at (21,87,57) — inside mine_stair zone (z54-60), the corridor Grog was told to
have exclusive anti-clump claim on this mission. Dig-law correctly allowed it (mine_stair IS a
legit zone, just not MY assigned one) but the mission brief's "don't enter the stairwell" rule has
no code enforcement, only driver discipline — a plain `/mine` with a wide maxDistance doesn't know
or care which zone a candidate sits in beyond the dig-law pass/fail. Checked player positions right
after (bot.entities scan) — Grog was 54.7 blocks away at (46.7,38,54.5), already deep past this
shallow spot, so no actual collision/interference happened, just an unintended zone trespass.
Then hit a real stuck: goto back out failed twice (`ashfinder: no path`, then `gotoLoopPf` 5x
false-reach). Ran the diagnostic properly this time instead of assuming wedge: raw jump test gave
a small but NONZERO delta (0.05, onGround:false) — not full-wedge. Followed the taxonomy's actual
fix (face the open direction, forward+jump held together) and got 4 real blocks of movement +
a ~2.5 block fall (open air had been dug/exposed on both x-sides of the spot) — confirms this was
a false-reach/no-path goto limitation on a real, physically fine bot, not a client freeze. Landed
at (25.7,84,57.3), still inside mine_stair's footprint and now sealed (canDig:false correctly
refuses to path out of the self-made pocket, matches the already-logged "legacy dig-pocket
unescapable" pattern — except this one's fresh, not pre-fix). Used `/trigger home` (sanctioned
self-rescue, ~4min after the last home-trigger so spacing was fine) — worked instantly, zero
issue. Suggest: (1) `/mine`'s candidate search should accept an optional zone-name filter (or a
tighter maxDistance from a position solidly inside the driver's own assigned zone) so a wide-radius
mine call can't wander into a DIFFERENT zone that happens to also pass dig-law; (2) worth a BASE.md
hazard-style note for the (20-26,83-87,56-58) pocket area near the mine_stair entrance since it's
now demonstrated to open into unexpected air gaps close to the surface.

input.message:
branchMine trunk 22/22 completed clean, zero incidents in the scar zone (your patch held perfectly, walked/dug straight through x44->x24). BUT: zero iron_ore found. Two real problems, both structural not random:

1. branchMine's "y" param is metadata-only, does NOT descend the bot - confirmed via result.trunk: from y54 to y53, basically flat the whole 22-step run. We stayed at hub level (y53-54) the entire time, never reached the actual y49-50 iron band. Matches skills.js's own comment ("y itself isn't used to move the bot... caller is expected to already be at depth"). Whoever's next branchmine call needs to actually descend to y49 first (buildStaircase deeper, or manual dig-down) before calling branchmine, not just pass y as a label.

2. Branches went the WRONG z-direction: trunk ran west at z~54-58, branches explored z46-51 (that's NORTH). Cluster 1 target is z66-67 - SOUTH of the trunk, opposite direction. So even at the right y, my branches wouldn't have reached it.

Net result: got a big copper haul instead (raw_copper 42 total, ores.copper_ore:8 this run) plus pointed_dripstone x8 + dripstone_block x3 (dripstone pocket in-path). Zero iron banked.

TOOL CHECK per your new law: stone_pickaxe DIED mid-run (was 34%, called it) - inventory now shows ZERO pickaxes of any kind, confirmed via eval. Can't mine further until re-tooled. No wood/sticks on hand to craft down here either.

PLAN: heading back up now to bank the copper at chest D + hit chest B for a pickaxe (iron if Grog banked one per your note, else stone). Will report chest readback + ask for corrected branchmine params (deeper start + south-facing) before the next cluster-1 attempt, or take reassignment if you want to replan the approach first.

Stopped the /mine iron_ore task after it dragged me way off course. Root cause: "nearest matching candidate" logic doesn't care about cluster/zone identity, just distance - from the staircase landing spot (34,48,63), Grog's cluster 2 (38-39,47-48,59-60) was CLOSER than my cluster 1 (25-26,49-50,66-67), so /mine went straight for cluster 2 instead. The "zone":"mine_grid" param didn't restrict candidates to a sub-area (mine_grid covers x14-80,z35-80,y45-62 - both clusters and then some, so it's a legality gate not a targeting filter).

Chased cluster-2 candidates for several minutes with a persistent, never-closing ~10-block VERTICAL false-reach gap (same bug family as Bonk's 1.8h one, but much bigger and vertical) - ended up relocated far off (last stop: 42.6,38,43.4, y38 which is BELOW mine_grid's own y45 floor). 0/16 iron gained the whole time. Bot is SAFE: hp20/food20, onGround true, standing on granite, open air on all 4 sides (real cave, not sealed), tools healthy (pick 91%, axe 100%, shovel 94%). Not a wedge, not danger - just wasted travel chasing the wrong cluster.

Also: this cluster-2 approach angle may be genuinely hard to reach (10-block vertical gaps on multiple different candidates there, not a fluke) - worth flagging for whenever Grog goes for it.

Holding here, not self-routing further. Options as I see them: (a) I walk back to ~x27-28 area (close to MY cluster1) first, then re-issue /mine iron_ore with a tight maxDistance (~10-12) so cluster2 can't out-compete on distance, or (b) you want to re-scope. Which way do you want this?

input.command:
prev=""
while true; do
  json=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3205/status)
  state=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask']['state'] if d.get('currentTask') else 'none')")
  detail=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask'].get('detail') if d.get('currentTask') else '')")
  y=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['pos']['y'])")
  hp=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['health'])")
  if [ "$detail" != "$prev" ]; then
    echo "PROGRESS detail=$detail y=$y hp=$hp state=$state"
    prev="$detail"
  fi
  if [ "$state" = "done" ] || [ "$state" = "failed" ]; then
    echo "TERMINAL state=$state detail=$detail y=$y hp=$hp"
    break
  fi
  sleep 15
done

## [open] /mine "zone" param is a legality gate, not a targeting filter — picks nearest candidate regardless of cluster — Thak, 2026-09-01
Dispatched `/mine {"block":"iron_ore","maxDistance":24,"zone":"mine_grid"}` from the staircase
landing spot (34,48,63), intending to hit MY assigned cluster 1 (25-26,49-50,66-67). Instead it
went straight for Grog's cluster 2 (38-39,47-48,59-60) — closer by raw distance from that spot
(~5.7 vs ~9.3 blocks) — and burned several minutes chasing it into a persistent, never-closing
~10-BLOCK VERTICAL false-reach gap (same bug family as the already-logged 1.8h horizontal one,
just much bigger and on the y-axis), eventually relocating the bot far off (y38, below mine_grid's
own y45 floor) with 0 iron gained. Root cause: `zone` only gates LEGALITY (is this position inside
a dig-law zone at all) — it does NOT restrict candidate search to a sub-area of that zone, and
mine_grid is one big box (x14-80,z35-80,y45-62) covering BOTH iron clusters plus everything
between them. mineBlocks' own "nearest match wins" logic has no concept of "which cluster am I
assigned to." Fix that worked: physically walk to within `maxDistance` of ONLY the intended
cluster first (so the other cluster falls outside the search radius entirely), then call `/mine`
with a TIGHT maxDistance (10 worked clean, got exactly 5/5 of cluster 1 in two passes, zero
detour). Suggest for the code backlog: a real `center`/`near` targeting param for `/mine` (filter
candidates by distance from a given point, not just from the bot's live position) so multi-cluster
zones don't need "which cluster is closest right now" driver math every time. Bonus data point:
cluster 2's repeated ~10-block vertical gaps (not a fluke — hit on 3+ different candidates there)
suggests it sits in/near the branchmine-scar cavern geometry — worth flagging for whoever mines it
next (matches "the scar eats pathfinding" from the earlier hazard alert).

input.command:
prev=""
while true; do
  json=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3205/status)
  state=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask']['state'] if d.get('currentTask') else 'none')")
  detail=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask'].get('detail') if d.get('currentTask') else '')")
  y=$(echo "$json" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['pos']['y'])")
  if [ "$detail" != "$prev" ]; then
    echo "PROGRESS detail=$detail y=$y state=$state"
    prev="$detail"
  fi
  if [ "$state" = "done" ] || [ "$state" = "failed" ]; then
    echo "TERMINAL state=$state detail=$detail y=$y"
    break
  fi
  sleep 15
done

## [open] genuinely undug rock corridor near cluster 3 → mineBlocks/buildStaircase both false-reach loop instead of digging through → real drowning incident — Thak, 2026-09-01
Cluster 3 (23-24,y46-47,77-79) sits 4-5 blocks past a wall of SOLID, NEVER-DUG stone from the
nearest reachable position — ground-truth blockAt scan confirmed z74-76 at x24,y45-49 were 100%
stone, no existing tunnel/cavity at all, not degraded terrain. Both `/staircase{toY:47}` and
`/mine{iron_ore,maxDistance:10-15}` tried repeatedly from a spot ~4 blocks short and produced the
exact same failure signature as the earlier false-reach bugs (goto "reached" with a persistent
1-6 block gap that never closes) — but this time the root cause is different: there's genuinely
NO PATH, period, because nothing has ever dug through that rock. Neither skill detected "this
requires digging a fresh corridor, not routing" — they just retried pathfinding forever against a
wall. Escalation-rule fix that worked: manual /eval `bot.dig()` straight down the corridor line
(equip pickaxe, dig 2-tall column each step, walk into the cleared cell) — reached the ore in
under a minute once done by hand instead of via skill retries.

WORSE: a water pocket sat at (24,47-48,73) right where I started digging, and standing there
mid-dig-loop caused a real DROWNING incident — 30+ suppressed "health dropped to 18" ring events
(server-suppressed duplicate spam, only the total drop was visible) cascading down to panic firing
at 7.67hp (`panic reflex firing`, health event 444). Runner's own panic-response caught it clean
(sealed 3 cobblestone, health regenerated to 20 within seconds) — the SAFETY NET worked exactly as
designed, this is not a panic-response bug. But the underlying cause (standing in/near a small
water pocket during a long uninterrupted bot.dig() loop with no oxygen/isInWater check) could have
been avoided: dug the SAME corridor one y-level lower (y45-46 instead of y46-47) on the retry and
it was bone dry the whole way, zero further incident. Also notable: the water had fully drained
away by the time I re-checked (open path = drains), so a driver hitting this same wall later might
not even see the hazard that bit me.

Suggest: (1) mineBlocks/buildStaircase should distinguish "no path exists yet" (needs digging) from
"path exists but pathfinder can't compute/execute it" (the classic false-reach case) and dig a
straight corridor toward an out-of-reach-but-legal-zone ore target instead of retry-looping; (2) any
`/eval` bot.dig() loop that runs more than a couple seconds should check `bot.entity.isInWater` /
`bot.oxygenLevel` between steps and bail/surface if either goes bad, rather than trusting the panic
reflex as the only safety net; (3) worth an isInWater/oxygenLevel check added to the generic

## [open] genuinely undug rock corridor near cluster 3 → mineBlocks/buildStaircase both false-reach loop instead of digging through → real drowning incident — Thak, 2026-09-01
Cluster 3 (23-24,y46-47,77-79) sits 4-5 blocks past a wall of SOLID, NEVER-DUG stone from the
nearest reachable position — ground-truth blockAt scan confirmed z74-76 at x24,y45-49 were 100%
stone, no existing tunnel/cavity at all, not degraded terrain. Both `/staircase{toY:47}` and
`/mine{iron_ore,maxDistance:10-15}` tried repeatedly from a spot ~4 blocks short and produced the
exact same failure signature as the earlier false-reach bugs (goto "reached" with a persistent
1-6 block gap that never closes) — but this time the root cause is different: there's genuinely
NO PATH, period, because nothing has ever dug through that rock. Neither skill detected "this
requires digging a fresh corridor, not routing" — they just retried pathfinding forever against a
wall. Escalation-rule fix that worked: manual /eval `bot.dig()` straight down the corridor line
(equip pickaxe, dig 2-tall column each step, walk into the cleared cell) — reached the ore in
under a minute once done by hand instead of via skill retries.

WORSE: a water pocket sat at (24,47-48,73) right where I started digging, and standing there
mid-dig-loop caused a real DROWNING incident — 30+ suppressed "health dropped to 18" ring events
(server-suppressed duplicate spam, only the total drop was visible) cascading down to panic firing
at 7.67hp (`panic reflex firing`, health event 444). Runner's own panic-response caught it clean
(sealed 3 cobblestone, health regenerated to 20 within seconds) — the SAFETY NET worked exactly as
designed, this is not a panic-response bug. But the underlying cause (standing in/near a small
water pocket during a long uninterrupted bot.dig() loop with no oxygen/isInWater check) could have
been avoided: dug the SAME corridor one y-level lower (y45-46 instead of y46-47) on the retry and
it was bone dry the whole way, zero further incident. Also notable: the water had fully drained
away by the time I re-checked (open path = drains), so a driver hitting this same wall later might
not even see the hazard that bit me.

Suggest: (1) mineBlocks/buildStaircase should distinguish "no path exists yet" (needs digging) from
"path exists but pathfinder can't compute/execute it" (the classic false-reach case) and dig a
straight corridor toward an out-of-reach-but-legal-zone ore target instead of retry-looping; (2) any
`/eval` bot.dig() loop that runs more than a couple seconds should check `bot.entity.isInWater` /
`bot.oxygenLevel` between steps and bail/surface if either goes bad, rather than trusting the panic
reflex as the only safety net; (3) worth an isInWater/oxygenLevel check added to the generic
runTargetWithWatchdog used by staircase/branchmine/mineBlocks too, same reasoning.

Full writeup + 3 suggested code fixes in FEEDBACK.md (mineBlocks/staircase should recognize "no path exists, needs digging" vs false-reach; eval dig-loops should oxygen/water-check; watchdogs should too).

   d) **Full-wedge incident**: hit a genuine full-wedge, ran the FEEDBACK-documented stuck-taxonomy diagnostic, escalated for hard restart per doctrine, then self-rescued via `/trigger home` post-restart per team-lead's exact ladder instructions.

   e) **Mission completion + report**: banked 7 coal + 13 raw_copper to chest D (readback-verified), sent DEPOT lines, reported full mission summary to team-lead.

   f) **DEEP IRON, CLUSTER 1 mission** (team-lead's 2nd major assignment): withdraw torches/pickaxe from chest B, route down staircase entrance→hub, ground-truth staircase walkability (bonus deliverable), `/branchmine{y:49}` aiming west toward cluster 1, watch for void behavior (y-poll 15s, /stop on drop>2 — testing a new dig-support fix's first live run), bank iron/coal, report route walkability + branchmine void behavior + iron count + quirks.

   g) **URGENT SAFETY HOLD** (team-lead interrupt): stop at hub, do not travel/branchmine west of x40 due to a persistent terrain scar (36-39,y37-54,z57-62) that eats pathfinding (3 falls, health to 5 each time); report position immediately if already west of x40 or fallen, do not self-route.

   h) **CORRIDOR CLEAR** (team-lead follow-up): scar patched by Grog, resume cluster-1 mission with same brief, trust the dig-support guard but keep 15s watch.

   i) **NEW LAW: post-task checklist** (chief decree, mid-task): after every task cycle — tool durability check (<30% → re-kit), stock glance vs minimums (iron_ingot 64/target 280, coal 64, torch 64, planks 64, logs 64, sticks 32, bread 40, cobble 128, saplings 16), deficit in own lane (ORE) → next target, decide while walking.

   j) **NEW LAW: TODO.md = live task board** (chief decree): board is single task source; claim rows (Status→DOING+botname), execute, mark DONE with ground-truth note, take next; roles soft; add rows for found deficits.

   k) **Corrected branchmine plan** (team-lead, after I reported branchMine's y-param-doesn't-descend + wrong-branch-direction bugs, 0 iron result, and dead pickaxe): bank copper/dripstone + re-tool (iron pick from chest B if Grog banked one, else stone) → staircase down to hub → walk west to ~(27,54,64) → fresh `/staircase{toY:49}` → targeted `/mine{block:iron_ore,count:16,maxDistance:24,zone:mine_grid}` → bank, report.

   m) **Cluster 1 completed**: 5/5 iron_ore mined, banked, reported. Board updated: row #1 DONE, row #3 (cluster 3) self-claimed as DOING (avoiding row #2/cluster-2 per team-lead's caution about the scar/BariBrute assignment).

   n) **Cluster 3 self-directed execution** (following the now-proven pattern from cluster 1, no new team-lead instruction needed): staircase+targeted mine approach; hit and resolved a genuine "no tunnel exists, must dig by hand" situation plus a real drowning incident (handled via panic-response + manual redig one y-level lower); mined 8/16 iron (more than the original 5-block scan estimated); banked, reported, re-kitted (crafted fresh stone_pickaxe since old one hit 34% durability), updated board/BASE.md.

   Throughout, standing operational laws to uphold (from DRIVER_GUIDE.md and team-lead's decrees): poll every 15-30s (never faster), one task at a time, ground-truth verify everything (never trust chat narration or a skill's own "ok:true"), `/collect {radius:24}` after every gather task, DEPOT ledger lines via `/chat` after every deposit/withdraw with readback-verification (a chest-full deposit can fail silently with an empty array per Bonk's gotcha — always readback), route to chest D via Mine House door (17,89-90,59) only, never cross (13,86-88,56), anti-clump (don't enter Grog's staircase/mine_stair corridor unless explicitly told), escalation rule (2 fails on same objective → drop to /eval or report, don't blind-retry), tp/RCON teleports BANNED (use `/trigger home` self-rescue instead, with ~15s+ spacing between uses, and a 10s+ settle wait after any runner restart before trusting a raw-control probe), stuck-taxonomy diagnostic order (check nearby entities → raw jump/forward control test → check recent blink) before escalating a "stuck" report, FEEDBACK.md entries logged the moment a quirk/bug is found (append-only, format: `## [open|shipped] title — BotName, date` + symptom/evidence/fix), caveman output style active for all my text responses to the human/team relay.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Mineflayer-based bot runner architecture: HTTP API (`GET /status`, `POST /goto`, `/mine`, `/chop`, `/collect`, `/deposit`, `/withdraw`, `/craft`, `/chat`, `/eval`, `/staircase`, `/branchmine`, `/stop`, `/relog`, `/idleguard`, `GET /events?since=N`)

   - Stuck-in-place taxonomy (3 signatures): TORN-GOTO (runner blink mid-edit), FULL-WEDGE (zero position delta on ANY raw control incl. jump — needs relog then hard restart + `/trigger home`), STEP-SNAG (partial/inconsistent real movement — rebuild tread or reroute)
   - Panic reflex: auto-fires at hp<8, aborts task, either flees to camp (close/shallow) or seals in place + eats (far/deep) — confirmed working exactly as designed during a drowning incident
   - `/trigger sethome` / `/trigger home` (cavehome datapack) — driven via `/eval` `bot.chat("/trigger ...")`, not `/chat`; needs ~15s+ spacing between calls; works reliably post-hard-restart if given 10s+ settle time first

   - Vec3 construction in `/eval` sandbox: no `require()` available; use `bot.entity.position.constructor` (aliased `V`) to build `new V(x,y,z)` since `Vec3` isn't a global
   - `/eval` scope: `(bot, mcData, skills, log)` only — `log` is a reserved identifier, caused one `SyntaxError: Identifier 'log' has already been declared` which I fixed by renaming my local variable to `trace`
   - Manual corridor digging pattern (escalation-rule fallback when a skill genuinely can't find/execute a path because no tunnel exists yet): equip pickaxe, loop `bot.dig()` on each solid block in a straight line, `bot.lookAt()` + `setControlState("forward",true)` briefly to step into the cleared cell, repeat

   - Caveman output style is ACTIVE for this entire session (system-reminder confirmed) — all my chat/report text should be terse/compressed

3. Files and Code Sections:

"genuinely undug rock corridor near cluster 3 → mineBlocks/buildStaircase both false-reach loop instead of digging through → real drowning incident" — `[open]`, 3 suggested code fixes (distinguish no-path-exists from false-reach; eval dig-loops should check isInWater/oxygenLevel; watchdogs should too)

addedLines: - cavecrew-builder: Bounded implementation worker — edits 1-2 files per task with exact instructions. Use for scoped edits, not open-ended features. Returns caveman-compressed report — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-investigator: Locate code, trace symbols, map subsystems. Read-only hunter. Use instead of vanilla Explore when answer is "where is X / how does X flow". Returns caveman-compressed findings — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-reviewer: Diff review — correctness bugs, edge cases, dumb waste. Point at a diff, branch, or file set. Returns caveman-compressed findings ranked by severity — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	# BARITONE.md — heavy-lifter bots: headless real-client + Baritone
2	
3	Blueprint for adding Baritone-driven REAL Minecraft Java clients alongside the
4	mineflayer fleet. Mineflayer stays primary; baritone bots are ADDITIONAL
5	heavy-lifters for long-haul pathing, bulk mining, and big travel. Prototype
6	bot: **BariBrute**.
7	
8	Decision date: 2026-09-01. Verdict: **PATH 1 — HeadlessMc + official Baritone
9	v1.17.0** (real cabaletta release, built FOR 1.21.11, Fabric supported).
10	Community forks (Nevarielle, chasteboymc-boop) are obsolete — skip. Minosoft
11	(no baritone hook) and Automatone (server-side mod, violates client-only
12	spirit) rejected.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. Chosen stack — exact versions + URLs
17	
18	| Component | Version | URL |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar` |
21	| Baritone (official, standalone fabric) | v1.17.0 | `https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` |
22	| hmc-specifics (console→game control wire) | 1.21.11-fabric, mod 2.4.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar` |
23	| Fabric API | match 1.21.11 (~0.141.3+1.21.11) | pull via HMC `mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api` (Modrinth) — safer than hand-URL |
24	| Java | 21 (already installed) | `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe` |
25	
26	Fallback if hmc-specifics jar clashes with baritone at mod load (rare): drop
27	hmc-specifics, relaunch with `-commands` flag (built-in headlessmc-runtime,
28	weaker console — basic chat send still works). That is PATH 2; try only if
29	PATH 1 breaks.
30	
31	Known non-issue: server-side plugin "BaritoneRemover" exists in the wild and
32	kicks baritone users — irrelevant here, our own localhost server, not
33	installed.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 2. Install layout — `C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\`
38	
39	Per-bot directory = per-bot game dir. Each launcher runs with cwd set to its
40	bot dir so `.minecraft\logs\latest.log` (the state channel) and
41	`.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` are isolated per bot. Disk cost of the
42	duplicated version files is accepted for isolation.
43	
44	```
45	C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\
46	  baritone-runner.mjs                  <- HTTP wrapper (this blueprint, part 4)
47	  shared\                              <- downloaded jars, copied into each bot
48	    headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
49	    baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
50	    hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
51	  bots\BariBrute\                      <- cwd for BariBrute's launcher process
52	    headlessmc-launcher.jar            (copy from shared)
53	    .minecraft\
54	      mods\                            (fabric-api + baritone + hmc-specifics)
55	      logs\latest.log                  (state channel — wrapper tails this)
56	      baritone\settings.txt            (safety config, pre-written by wrapper)
57	  pids\  logs\                         <- wrapper-level, same shape as cave/
58	```
59	
60	### Install steps (one-time, PowerShell)
61	
62	```powershell
63	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
64	New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\BariBrute
65	cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
66	curl.exe -L -o headlessmc-launcher.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
67	curl.exe -L -o baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
68	curl.exe -L -o hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
69	copy headlessmc-launcher.jar ..\bots\BariBrute\
70	
71	# interactive first-run inside bot dir (installs fabric + fabric-api):
72	cd ..\bots\BariBrute
73	& "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe" -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar
74	```
75	
76	Inside the HMC console, one line at a time:
77	
78	```
79	config --property hmc.offline.username=BariBrute
80	fabric 1.21.11
81	mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api
82	specifics fabric:1.21.11 hmc-specifics
83	```
84	
85	If `specifics` doesn't know 1.21.11 yet, hand-copy instead. Baritone always
86	needs hand-copy (not on Modrinth):
87	
88	```powershell
89	copy ..\..\shared\baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar .minecraft\mods\
90	copy ..\..\shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar .minecraft\mods\   # only if specifics cmd failed
91	```
92	
93	### Launch line (what the wrapper sends after boot, or manual test)
94	
95	```
96	launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline -lwjgl --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Djava.awt.headless=true" --game-args "--quickPlayMultiplayer localhost:25565"
97	```
98	
99	- `-offline` + `hmc.offline.username` = no Microsoft OAuth (server is
100	  offline-mode, matches).
101	- `-lwjgl` = headless LWJGL patch, no window.
102	- `--quickPlayMultiplayer` = auto-join, zero GUI clicking.
103	
104	---
105	
106	## 3. Control + feedback channels
107	
108	**Command wire (in):** launcher process stdin. hmc-specifics adds console
109	words once the game is loaded: `msg <text>` (send chat exactly like a player),
110	plus `connect`/`disconnect` and `/` for slash commands. A `#`-prefixed chat
111	line is intercepted CLIENT-SIDE by Baritone (`chatControl` setting, on by
112	default) before it leaves for the server — baritone commands never appear in
113	real server chat.
114	
115	```
116	msg #goto 100 64 200
117	msg #mine 64 iron_ore
118	msg #stop
119	```
120	
121	**Feedback wire (out):** NOT the HMC console — the client's own
122	`.minecraft\logs\latest.log`. Baritone replies go to the local chat HUD only,
123	and vanilla logs HUD lines with the `[CHAT]` marker. Tail that file, regex:

148	
149	Same shape as `cave/runner.js`: one process per bot, HTTP control API on
150	127.0.0.1, state polled not pushed. Difference: no in-process mineflayer
151	object — this is a **process-pipe + log-tail driver** around an external JVM.
152	
153	```
154	node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 [--host localhost --mcport 25565]
155	```
156	
157	**Port registry:** baritone heavy-lifters own **3301-3309** (mineflayer keeps
158	3200-3299 per CIV.md — add a cross-note there). BariBrute = 3301.
159	
160	**Boot sequence:**
161	1. Pre-write `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` with the safety block (part 5)
162	   — config-file level, survives relaunch, no chat-push race.
163	2. `spawn('C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-21.0.10\\bin\\java.exe', ['-jar','headlessmc-launcher.jar'], { cwd: BOT_DIR, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] })`
164	3. Write the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line (part 2) to stdin.
165	4. Start log tail (fs.watch + read-from-last-offset on
166	   `.minecraft\logs\latest.log`); wait for join marker before accepting tasks.
167	5. Send `msg #set chatDebug true`.

169	**HTTP surface (mirrors cave/runner.js task-endpoint shape):**
170	
171	| Endpoint | Body | Action |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /goto` | `{x,y,z}` | no-go gate → `msg #goto x y z` |
174	| `POST /mine` | `{block,count}` | `msg #mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings) |
175	| `POST /tunnel` | `{h,w,d}` | no-go gate on projected end → `msg #tunnel h w d` |
176	| `POST /farm` | `{range}` | `msg #farm <range>` |
177	| `POST /follow` | `{player}` | `msg #follow <player>` |
178	| `POST /stop` | — | `msg #stop` |
179	| `POST /relog` | — | hmc-specifics `disconnect` + `connect`; full JVM relaunch if that fails |
180	| `GET /status` | — | `{name, position, task, lastBaritoneLine, connected, uptime}` from parsed log state |

203	legitMine false                # CHIEF RULING 2026-09-01 — parity with mineflayer's chunk-scan /mine (was: true, honest visible-only)
204	allowDownward false           # never mine block under own feet (fall-safety, matches fleet doctrine)
205	minYLevelWhileMining -54      # floor: stay above bedrock chaos
206	maxYLevelWhileMining 95       # ceiling: all ore-hunting stays BELOW both bases (camp y~89 surface, FEL y=111)
207	blocksToDisallowBreaking [chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel]
208	shortBaritonePrefix true      # "[B]" — stable short tag for the log regex
209	chatDebug true                # belt+braces with the boot msg push
210	```
211	
212	### 5b. FEL no-go zone (-3, 111, 4) ±15 — WRAPPER-LEVEL, MANDATORY
213	
214	**Baritone has NO native coordinate keep-out zone.** Verified upstream:
215	issues #2597 ("Blacklisted zones"), #3847 ("safearea/No break zone"), #1165
216	("Blacklisting coordinates") — all open, never shipped. `#blacklist` only
217	skips the single closest matched block; `#sel` is a build-area selector, not
218	an exclusion. So the wrapper enforces, two layers:
219	
220	**Layer 1 — command gate.** Every coordinate-bearing task (`/goto`, `/tunnel`
221	projected end, future `/goal`) is checked before piping. Reject with HTTP 403
222	if the target lands inside the padded full-height column:
223	
224	```js
225	const NOGO = { x: -3, z: 4, r: 15, pad: 5 };   // padded box: x [-23,17], z [-16,24], all y
226	function inNoGo(x, z) {
227	  return x >= NOGO.x - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && x <= NOGO.x + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad
228	      && z >= NOGO.z - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && z <= NOGO.z + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad;
229	}
230	```
231	
232	Full-height column (not a y-slab): break-capable pathing under or over the
233	FEL base is foundation risk, not worth the shortcut.
234	
235	**Layer 2 — position watchdog.** `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` take no coords
236	and a legal `#goto` can still PATH THROUGH the zone (baritone cannot be told
237	to route around it). So the log-tail position parser doubles as watchdog:
238	parsed position inside the padded box → immediately `msg #stop`, then
239	`msg #goto <camp waypoint>`, mark task `aborted:nogo` in `/status`, log loud.
240	Watchdog is the backstop; the gate is the front door. Drivers should also
241	prefer targets whose straight line to the bot doesn't cross the box.

295	## Upstream status 2026-09-01
296	
297	Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
298	to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
299	forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform
300	in minecraft:blur/0" through "blur/5"; (2) hmc-specifics' JLine console
301	misbehaves when stdio is a plain pipe (no TTY), as the wrapper needs.
302	
303	### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms
304	
305	Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
306	uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
307	grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
308	`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
309	non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
310	bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
311	to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
312	and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
313	abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
314	(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
315	come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).
316	
317	Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
318	release:
319	- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
320	  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
321	  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
322	  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
323	  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
324	  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
325	  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
326	  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
327	- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
328	  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
329	  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
330	- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
331	  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
332	  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
333	- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
334	  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
335	- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
336	  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
337	  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
338	  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
339	  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
340	- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
341	  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
342	  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
343	  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.
344	
345	**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
346	own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
347	patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
348	More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
349	real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
350	over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
351	real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
352	gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
353	game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
354	redirection layer at all.
355	- hmc-specifics' console (`msg`, `connect`, `gui`, `click`) is confirmed to
356	  work identically with or without `-lwjgl` — see maintainer replies in
357	  [issue #230](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/230) and
358	  [issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390). Baritone
359	  chat-command control (part 3 of this doc) is unaffected by dropping the
360	  flag.
361	- Trade-off: a real (small, minimizable) game window per bot instance, and a
362	  sliver of real GPU/VRAM per client instead of zero. JVM heap budget in part
363	  6 is unaffected (that's CPU RAM, not GPU).
364	- If this stack ever moves to a true headless Linux box with no GPU at all,
365	  the Linux-native equivalent is Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe (software GL) in front
366	  of an un-patched launch — a working docker recipe is in
367	  [issue #249](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/249) (needs
368	  the `x11-xserver-utils` package per maintainer 3arthqu4ke, plus
369	  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Not directly usable on bare Windows (no X11);
370	  would need WSL2. Untested by this pass — field-verify separately if needed.
371	- If dropping `-lwjgl` is rejected and true headless is a hard requirement:
372	  this bucket is "fixable soon, not now" — file a new upstream issue with the
373	  exact blur/uniform log lines + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric. The
374	  maintainers (okafke, 3arthqu4ke) have a strong track record on this exact
375	  bug family — #388/#389 to merged fixes #406/#407 the same day.

377	### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)
378	
379	Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
380	[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
381	"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
382	reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
383	reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
384	`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
385	section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").
386	
387	Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
388	`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
389	separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
390	guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
391	is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
392	that way.
393	
394	`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
395	one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
396	a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
397	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
398	  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
399	  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
400	- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
401	  version of the above.
402	
403	No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
404	ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
405	maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
406	reason to stand up a pty shim.
407	
408	**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
409	(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
410	from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.

526	  at me.earth.headlessmc.mc.jline.VersionAgnosticJLineCommandLineReader.hackInTerminal
527	```
528	
529	Root cause, confirmed: **this is a second, separate JLine console — inside
530	the GAME process itself**, distinct from the launcher's own JLine (which
531	already auto-negotiates `dumb` terminal mode fine over the piped stdin, per
532	`headlessmc.log`: `JLine Terminal type: dumb`). Under PATH 1 (hmc-specifics,
533	no `-commands`), hmc-specifics mixes into `Minecraft.<init>` and spins up
534	*another* JLine reader inside the child JVM to read further stdin — and this
535	one is NOT auto-falling back to dumb mode, so it crashes trying to build a
536	real Windows console terminal over what is, from the child JVM's point of
537	view, a fully piped/non-console stdin (the launcher relays commands to it,
538	the child JVM's own stdin isn't a real console handle at all).
539	
540	Two upstream fixes attempted, from this doc's own recommended order:
541	
542	- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true`, passed as a `--jvm -D` flag on the
543	  `launch` line (confirmed present verbatim in the child JVM's actual
544	  cmdline via `headlessmc.log`'s `ProcessFactory` entry) — **did not help,
545	  identical crash, same stack trace.** The dumb-mode flag doesn't prevent
546	  the crash; whatever this code path does, it fails before or regardless of
547	  checking that property.
548	- `hmc.jline.enabled=false`, same way (`--jvm "-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"`)
549	  — **this worked.** No crash. Game proceeded past `SpecificsInitializer.init`
550	  straight through mod loading, asset/texture atlas creation, and the
551	  blur-uniform WARNs, into a live render loop. This is the confirmed fix for
552	  this blocker — use `hmc.jline.enabled=false` directly, don't bother trying
553	  the dumb-mode flag first for this exact crash (leave the recommendation in
554	  the section above as-is for the general JLine-over-pipe case; this specific
555	  in-game-JLine-during-Minecraft-init crash needs the harder disable).
556	
557	**Doc update:** for PATH 1 (hmc-specifics loaded), pass
558	`-Dhmc.jline.enabled=false` on the `--jvm` launch flag from the very first
559	attempt. `config.properties`-level settings do not reliably reach the child
560	game JVM's flags (only some launcher-level settings like offline username
561	do) — always prefer the `--jvm -D` route for anything that needs to affect
562	the spawned Minecraft process specifically.
563	
564	### Third blocker found this round — game stalls forever, never attempts to join, window-visibility-independent
565	
566	With both above fixes applied (baritone+specifics installed, offline
567	username persisted, `hmc.jline.enabled=false`), the game **no longer
568	crashes** but also **never connects**. It reaches the render loop, logs the
569	harmless Realms-auth-401 and `blur/0`-`blur/5` WARNs, and then goes
570	completely silent — no `Connecting to`, no `Encryption`, no world-load line,
571	nothing — while the process stays alive, "responding" flickers between
572	`Running`/`Not Responding` in `tasklist`, and CPU time creeps up by roughly
573	1 second of CPU per 30-40 seconds of wall time (consistent with an idle
574	title-screen render loop doing near-nothing, not a deadlock or a spin).
575	`jstack` on the stalled process during the first occurrence confirmed the
576	render thread is in a completely ordinary `Thread.sleep` inside
577	`Minecraft.render`/`run` (`class_310.method_1523`/`method_1514`) — i.e. it
578	genuinely is just idling at whatever screen it's on, not blocked/deadlocked
579	on anything catchable in a thread dump. `--quickPlayMultiplayer
580	localhost:25565` never appears to fire, or fires and fails completely
581	silently with zero log trace either way.
582	
583	This was reproduced **twice, identically**, under two different window-
584	visibility strategies, ruling out the visibility angle as the cause:
585	
586	1. **Fully hidden window** (`ShowWindowAsync(hwnd, SW_HIDE)` applied to any
587	   new java window once created) — stalled at this exact point, confirmed
588	   via live `jstack` thread dump (killed by the coordinator after ~170s
589	   observed with zero progress).
590	2. **Minimized window** (`ShowWindowAsync(hwnd, SW_MINIMIZE)` instead,
591	   theorized as safer since DWM keeps compositing/presenting minimized
592	   windows unlike fully hidden ones) — **stalled identically**, same log
593	   line count frozen at the same `blur/5` point, same slow CPU creep, no
594	   RCON-visible join after 90+ seconds of polling. This falsifies the
595	   "hidden window starves the GPU swapchain" hypothesis from earlier in this
596	   session — minimized behaves the same as hidden, so window visibility
597	   state is not the variable causing the stall.
598	
599	Neither attempt ever produced a visible client window at any point (both
600	began life immediately with the window creation followed within ~3s by a
601	hide/minimize pass), so the no-visible-client law was never violated by this
602	session, and both attempts were killed cleanly with no client left
603	connected or visible.
604	
605	**What this narrows the cause down to** (untested, for the next session):
606	something in the PATH 1 stack (hmc-specifics init running inside
607	`Minecraft.<init>` via mixin, possibly interacting with how quickPlay is
608	scheduled relative to that mixin hook) either never fires the quickPlay
609	auto-connect at all, or fires it into a silent failure. Candidates worth
610	testing next, cheapest first:
611	- Manual connect instead of relying on `--quickPlayMultiplayer`: once the
612	  hmc-specifics console is confirmed alive in-game (it should be, since the
613	  crash that used to block it is fixed), drive it with `msg #include`... no
614	  — more directly, use the vanilla `connect <host>` hmc-specifics console
615	  word (or navigate the menu via `click`/`gui` console words documented for
616	  hmc-specifics) instead of the `--quickPlayMultiplayer` game arg, to see if
617	  the stall is specific to the quickPlay code path vs. multiplayer joining
618	  in general.
619	- Compare against PATH 2 (`-commands`, no hmc-specifics) with `-lwjgl`
620	  dropped: round 1's `hmc-launch2.mjs`/`hmc-launch3.mjs` runs (PATH 2, no
621	  baritone installed at the time) reached the exact same `blur/5` point and
622	  were also never confirmed to actually join before being externally killed
623	  — so this stall may predate this round's PATH-1-specific changes entirely
624	  and be a `--quickPlayMultiplayer` + HeadlessMc issue in general, not
625	  specific to hmc-specifics. Re-test PATH 2 now that baritone/mods are
626	  correctly installed, to isolate whether hmc-specifics is actually involved
627	  at all.
628	- Try omitting `--quickPlayMultiplayer` entirely and driving a manual
629	  multiplayer connect through hmc-specifics' `click`/`gui` console words
630	  once at the title screen, to bypass whatever quickPlay's internal state
631	  machine is stuck on.
632	- Capture a `jstack` dump specifically at the moment `--quickPlayMultiplayer`
633	  should be firing (right after title screen init) rather than after the
634	  fact, to see if a connect thread is present but parked, vs. never spawned.
635	
636	### Cleanup performed
637	
638	All BariBrute-round-2 java/node processes killed (launcher, game JVM, and
639	the `hmc-launch7.mjs` node wrapper) — verified via `tasklist`/`Get-Process`
640	that no stray processes remain and that the real server (PID 13908,
641	`fabric-server-launch`) was never touched. Left in place for next session
642	(real progress, do not undo): the mods copied into
643	`%APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods\` (`baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar`,
644	`hmc-specifics-1.21.11-2.4.0-fabric-release.jar`), and
645	`bots\BariBrute\HeadlessMC\config.properties`'s added
646	`hmc.offline.username=BariBrute` / `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true`
647	lines (harmless even though the dumb-mode one didn't end up mattering).
648	`hmc-launch4.mjs` through `hmc-launch7.mjs` in `baritone-lifter\` record the
649	exact progression of fixes tried, in order, for the next session to resume
650	from `hmc-launch7.mjs`'s approach (drop the window-hide/minimize step first
651	since it's now shown to be irrelevant to the stall; focus directly on the
652	quickPlay-vs-manual-connect question above).
653	
654	**No visible game client was ever left running.** BariBrute is not currently
655	connected to the fleet.
656	
657	---
658	
659	## Round 2 FINAL update — same session, 15-min hard cap — verdict: WORKS
660	
661	Coordinator's last card fixed it. Root cause of the "third blocker" above:
662	**`--quickPlayMultiplayer` itself is the broken piece, not window visibility,
663	not hmc-specifics, not jline.** Fix: drop `--quickPlayMultiplayer` from the
664	`launch` game-args entirely, boot to a plain title screen, then issue a
665	**manual connect** over the hmc-specifics console channel once the title
666	screen is up.
667	
668	### Exact working recipe
669	
670	1. Launch line (no quickPlay arg at all):
671	   ```
672	   launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Dhmc.jline.enabled=false"
673	   ```
674	2. Wait ~35s for title screen (real GPU render reaches the harmless
675	   blur-uniform WARNs by ~15-20s in; give it another 15s margin).
676	3. Send the connect command over the same stdin pipe:
677	   ```
678	   connect localhost 25565
679	   ```
680	   Exact syntax confirmed by decompiling `ConnectCommand.class` out of
681	   `hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar` with `javap -p -c` (no README/docs
682	   needed): `execute(String label, String... args)` requires `args.length > 1`
683	   ("Please specify an Ip!" otherwise), reads host from `args[1]`, and an
684	   optional port from `args[2]` (default 25565) — i.e. the raw console line is
685	   literally `connect <host> <port>`, space-separated, no flags.
686	4. Confirmed working end to end: client received the server's join/leave
687	   chat spam within ~15s of sending `connect`, and `node swarm/rcon.mjs
688	   "list"` (read-only, from `minecraft-mcp-v2`) showed `BariBrute` in the
689	   player list.
690	
691	**Doc update:** never use `--quickPlayMultiplayer` with this stack on this
692	MC/HMC version. Always boot plain and drive the join manually through
693	hmc-specifics' `connect` console word. This makes the earlier "candidates
694	for next session" list in the previous update moot — the first candidate
695	(manual connect instead of quickPlay) was the fix.
696	
697	### Baritone command channel — field-verified format
698	
699	Sent `msg #goto 60 90 120` over the launcher stdin once joined. Baritone
700	logged its own path plan to the launcher's stdout/log
701	(`[STDOUT]: Path goes for 76.69419795525604 blocks`) and began moving.
702	Confirmed movement via the fleet's own mineflayer bot HTTP eval endpoint
703	(`POST 127.0.0.1:3203/eval`, `bot.players['BariBrute'].entity.position`):
704	position went from `(3.5, 111, -6.5)` at spawn to `(11.97, 94, 48.45)` after
705	the goto fired — moving in the correct direction (x up, y down toward the
706	target's 90, z up toward the target's 120).
707	
708	Sent `msg #stop` next. Baritone answered on the in-game chat feedback
709	channel, format now pinned exactly:
710	```
711	[CHAT] [Baritone] > stop
712	[CHAT] [Baritone] ok canceled
713	```
714	(matches the `/\[CHAT\].*?\[(Baritone|B)\]\s*(.+)/` regex from part 3 of this
715	doc — `[Baritone]`, full word, not the short `[B]` form, at least for this
716	command; `shortBaritonePrefix` config wasn't active in this quick ad-hoc
717	test since it used the bare `launch`/`msg` commands rather than the full
718	`baritone-runner.mjs` wrapper's pre-written settings.txt). Position polled
719	again after `#stop` came back bit-for-bit identical
720	(`11.974708733124642, 94, 48.4548966911917`) confirming a clean, complete
721	halt with zero drift.
722	
723	### Safety incident — spawn point is inside the FEL no-go box, undetected by this ad-hoc script
724	
725	**BariBrute's server spawn point, `(3.5, 111, -6.5)`, is itself inside the
726	FEL no-go padded box** (`x∈[-23,17], z∈[-16,24]`, part 5b of this doc) — y=111
727	matches FEL's own y exactly. The quick `hmc-launch8.mjs` test script used for
728	this session's final attempt is a bare stdin/log-tail script with **no
729	no-go gate and no position watchdog** (those live in `baritone-runner.mjs`,
730	not in the throwaway `hmc-launch*.mjs` scripts used to iterate on the boot
731	sequence this session) — so `#goto 60 90 120` was sent and Baritone started
732	pathing from inside the FEL box with nothing checking it. It was stopped by
733	hand within seconds once the position readback showed the spawn coordinates,
734	before any real distance was covered, but the path was already crossing
735	close by the `[CAVE]` camp waypoint too (`(12, 89, 56)` per this doc's part
736	5c reference) — the position where it was actually stopped,
737	`(11.97, 94, 48.45)`, is only ~9 blocks from that camp point.
738	
739	**Action needed before any unattended/production use:** `baritone-runner.mjs`
740	already has both the no-go gate and the watchdog implemented (part 5b of
741	this doc) — this incident is purely because the quick ad-hoc `hmc-launch8.mjs`
742	test script doesn't wire through it, not a gap in the wrapper design. Next
743	session should either (a) drive BariBrute exclusively through
744	`baritone-runner.mjs` once it's updated with this session's fixes (drop
745	quickPlay, manual `connect`, `hmc.jline.enabled=false`), or (b) manually
746	`#goto` it to a known-clear waypoint immediately after any ad-hoc-script
747	session before leaving it running.
748	
749	### End state
750	
751	BariBrute was left **running and connected**, stopped (not pathing/mining),
752	at `(11.97, 94, 48.45)`. No visible window was shown at any point (hidden
753	via `ShowWindowAsync(SW_HIDE)` on the real GLFW window, applied within ~3s
754	of window creation, same as prior attempts this session).
755	
756	- Launcher java PID: 20240
757	- Game-client java PID: 33944
758	- Node wrapper (`hmc-launch8.mjs`) PID: 11196
759	- Real server (do not touch): PID 13908, untouched throughout
760	
761	**Verdict: WORKS.** Join, `#goto`, movement verification, and `#stop` all
762	confirmed end to end within the coordinator's 15-minute hard cap. Mining
763	test (`#mine cobblestone`, marked bonus/optional in the original task) was
764	skipped given the proximity-to-camp safety incident above and the time cap —
765	recommended as the first thing to try next session, from a repositioned,
766	verified-clear waypoint, through the real `baritone-runner.mjs` wrapper (so
767	the no-go watchdog is actually active) rather than another ad-hoc script.

# BARITONE.md — heavy-lifter bots: headless real-client + Baritone

Blueprint for adding Baritone-driven REAL Minecraft Java clients alongside the
mineflayer fleet. Mineflayer stays primary; baritone bots are ADDITIONAL
heavy-lifters for long-haul pathing, bulk mining, and big travel. Prototype
bot: **BariBrute**.

Decision date: 2026-09-01. Verdict: **PATH 1 — HeadlessMc + official Baritone
v1.17.0** (real cabaletta release, built FOR 1.21.11, Fabric supported).
Community forks (Nevarielle, chasteboymc-boop) are obsolete — skip. Minosoft
(no baritone hook) and Automatone (server-side mod, violates client-only
spirit) rejected.

---

## 1. Chosen stack — exact versions + URLs

| Component | Version | URL |
|---|---|---|
| HeadlessMc launcher | 2.10.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar` |
| Baritone (official, standalone fabric) | v1.17.0 | `https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar` |
| hmc-specifics (console→game control wire) | 1.21.11-fabric, mod 2.4.0 | `https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar` |
| Fabric API | match 1.21.11 (~0.141.3+1.21.11) | pull via HMC `mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api` (Modrinth) — safer than hand-URL |
| Java | 21 (already installed) | `C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe` |

Fallback if hmc-specifics jar clashes with baritone at mod load (rare): drop
hmc-specifics, relaunch with `-commands` flag (built-in headlessmc-runtime,
weaker console — basic chat send still works). That is PATH 2; try only if
PATH 1 breaks.

Known non-issue: server-side plugin "BaritoneRemover" exists in the wild and
kicks baritone users — irrelevant here, our own localhost server, not
installed.

---

## 2. Install layout — `C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\`

Per-bot directory = per-bot game dir. Each launcher runs with cwd set to its
bot dir so `.minecraft\logs\latest.log` (the state channel) and
`.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` are isolated per bot. Disk cost of the
duplicated version files is accepted for isolation.

```
C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\
  baritone-runner.mjs                  <- HTTP wrapper (this blueprint, part 4)
  shared\                              <- downloaded jars, copied into each bot
    headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
    baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
    hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
  bots\BariBrute\                      <- cwd for BariBrute's launcher process
    headlessmc-launcher.jar            (copy from shared)
    .minecraft\
      mods\                            (fabric-api + baritone + hmc-specifics)
      logs\latest.log                  (state channel — wrapper tails this)
      baritone\settings.txt            (safety config, pre-written by wrapper)
  pids\  logs\                         <- wrapper-level, same shape as cave/
```

### Install steps (one-time, PowerShell)

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\bots\BariBrute
cd C:\Users\phili\tools\baritone-lifter\shared
curl.exe -L -o headlessmc-launcher.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/releases/download/2.10.0/headlessmc-launcher-2.10.0.jar
curl.exe -L -o baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases/download/v1.17.0/baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar
curl.exe -L -o hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar https://github.com/headlesshq/hmc-specifics/releases/download/1.21.11-latest/hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar
copy headlessmc-launcher.jar ..\bots\BariBrute\

# interactive first-run inside bot dir (installs fabric + fabric-api):
cd ..\bots\BariBrute
& "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe" -jar headlessmc-launcher.jar
```

Inside the HMC console, one line at a time:

```
config --property hmc.offline.username=BariBrute
fabric 1.21.11
mod add fabric:1.21.11 fabric-api
specifics fabric:1.21.11 hmc-specifics
```

If `specifics` doesn't know 1.21.11 yet, hand-copy instead. Baritone always
needs hand-copy (not on Modrinth):

```powershell
copy ..\..\shared\baritone-standalone-fabric-1.17.0.jar .minecraft\mods\
copy ..\..\shared\hmc-specifics-1.21.11-fabric-latest.jar .minecraft\mods\   # only if specifics cmd failed
```

### Launch line (what the wrapper sends after boot, or manual test)

```
launch fabric:1.21.11 -offline -lwjgl --jvm "-Xmx3G -XX:+UseG1GC -Djava.awt.headless=true" --game-args "--quickPlayMultiplayer localhost:25565"
```

- `-offline` + `hmc.offline.username` = no Microsoft OAuth (server is
  offline-mode, matches).
- `-lwjgl` = headless LWJGL patch, no window.
- `--quickPlayMultiplayer` = auto-join, zero GUI clicking.

---

## 3. Control + feedback channels

**Command wire (in):** launcher process stdin. hmc-specifics adds console
words once the game is loaded: `msg <text>` (send chat exactly like a player),
plus `connect`/`disconnect` and `/` for slash commands. A `#`-prefixed chat
line is intercepted CLIENT-SIDE by Baritone (`chatControl` setting, on by
default) before it leaves for the server — baritone commands never appear in
real server chat.

```
msg #goto 100 64 200
msg #mine 64 iron_ore
msg #stop
```

**Feedback wire (out):** NOT the HMC console — the client's own
`.minecraft\logs\latest.log`. Baritone replies go to the local chat HUD only,
and vanilla logs HUD lines with the `[CHAT]` marker. Tail that file, regex:

```
/\[CHAT\].*?\[(Baritone|B)\]\s*(.+)/
```

At boot send `msg #set chatDebug true` for coordinate-bearing path/segment
debug lines (BetterBlockPos-shaped `(x,y,z)` text upstream — FIELD-VERIFY the
exact 1.17.0 string once live). Fallback position poll: `msg #eta` every few
seconds while a task runs, parse the reply line.

Baritone command surface (verified from cabaletta USAGE.md): `#goto x y z`,
`#goal`/`#path`, `#mine <count> <ore>`, `#follow <player>`, `#farm [range]`,
`#tunnel [h] [w] [d]`, `#build <schematic>`, `#explore`, `#stop`/`#cancel`/
`#forcecancel`, `#wp save/goal`, `#come`, `#find`, `#eta`, `#proc`. `#farm`
args beyond `<range> <waypoint>` unverified — field-check.

**No RCON anywhere in this path.** Commands in via client stdin-fed chat,
state out via client's own log file. The only RCON touch remains the
orchestrator's later cosmetic `team join` for the BariBrute name tag —
separate process, never through this wrapper. LAW.

---

## 4. Wrapper design — `baritone-runner.mjs`

Same shape as `cave/runner.js`: one process per bot, HTTP control API on
127.0.0.1, state polled not pushed. Difference: no in-process mineflayer
object — this is a **process-pipe + log-tail driver** around an external JVM.

```
node baritone-runner.mjs --name BariBrute --port 3301 [--host localhost --mcport 25565]
```

**Port registry:** baritone heavy-lifters own **3301-3309** (mineflayer keeps
3200-3299 per CIV.md — add a cross-note there). BariBrute = 3301.

**Boot sequence:**
1. Pre-write `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt` with the safety block (part 5)
   — config-file level, survives relaunch, no chat-push race.
2. `spawn('C:\\Program Files\\Java\\jdk-21.0.10\\bin\\java.exe', ['-jar','headlessmc-launcher.jar'], { cwd: BOT_DIR, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe'] })`
3. Write the `launch fabric:1.21.11 ...` line (part 2) to stdin.
4. Start log tail (fs.watch + read-from-last-offset on
   `.minecraft\logs\latest.log`); wait for join marker before accepting tasks.
5. Send `msg #set chatDebug true`.

**HTTP surface (mirrors cave/runner.js task-endpoint shape):**

| Endpoint | Body | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /goto` | `{x,y,z}` | no-go gate → `msg #goto x y z` |
| `POST /mine` | `{block,count}` | `msg #mine <count> <block>` (Y-clamped by settings) |
| `POST /tunnel` | `{h,w,d}` | no-go gate on projected end → `msg #tunnel h w d` |
| `POST /farm` | `{range}` | `msg #farm <range>` |
| `POST /follow` | `{player}` | `msg #follow <player>` |
| `POST /stop` | — | `msg #stop` |
| `POST /relog` | — | hmc-specifics `disconnect` + `connect`; full JVM relaunch if that fails |
| `GET /status` | — | `{name, position, task, lastBaritoneLine, connected, uptime}` from parsed log state |

`/status` and `/stop` semantics match what `overseer.mjs` already polls, so
the overseer can adopt BariBrute with one BOTS-array row (part 6).

---

## 5. Safety config

### 5a. Boot settings — written to `.minecraft\baritone\settings.txt`

**CHIEF RULING 2026-09-01: `legitMine` flipped OFF.** The mineflayer fleet's
own `/mine` already finds buried ore via chunk-data scans — visible-only was
holding Baritone to a *stricter* standard than the rest of the fleet, not a
stricter no-cheat law. Parity restored. All other safety settings
(`allowDownward`, y-clamps, `blocksToDisallowBreaking`) are UNCHANGED and
stay forever. First real-world data point behind the call: BariBrute's first
bulk-iron `/mine` job (legitMine=true) wandered ~790 blocks free-ranging
after visible-only candidates it could never path to, and finished with 0
iron per the server Ledger DB — see FEEDBACK.md's "iron manifest resolved"
entry.

```
legitMine false                # CHIEF RULING 2026-09-01 — parity with mineflayer's chunk-scan /mine (was: true, honest visible-only)
allowDownward false           # never mine block under own feet (fall-safety, matches fleet doctrine)
minYLevelWhileMining -54      # floor: stay above bedrock chaos
maxYLevelWhileMining 95       # ceiling: all ore-hunting stays BELOW both bases (camp y~89 surface, FEL y=111)
blocksToDisallowBreaking [chest,trapped_chest,crafting_table,furnace,blast_furnace,oak_sign,oak_wall_sign,barrel]

### 5b. FEL no-go zone (-3, 111, 4) ±15 — WRAPPER-LEVEL, MANDATORY

**Baritone has NO native coordinate keep-out zone.** Verified upstream:
issues #2597 ("Blacklisted zones"), #3847 ("safearea/No break zone"), #1165
("Blacklisting coordinates") — all open, never shipped. `#blacklist` only
skips the single closest matched block; `#sel` is a build-area selector, not
an exclusion. So the wrapper enforces, two layers:

**Layer 1 — command gate.** Every coordinate-bearing task (`/goto`, `/tunnel`
projected end, future `/goal`) is checked before piping. Reject with HTTP 403
if the target lands inside the padded full-height column:

```js
const NOGO = { x: -3, z: 4, r: 15, pad: 5 };   // padded box: x [-23,17], z [-16,24], all y
function inNoGo(x, z) {
  return x >= NOGO.x - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && x <= NOGO.x + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad
      && z >= NOGO.z - NOGO.r - NOGO.pad && z <= NOGO.z + NOGO.r + NOGO.pad;
}
```

Full-height column (not a y-slab): break-capable pathing under or over the
FEL base is foundation risk, not worth the shortcut.

**Layer 2 — position watchdog.** `#mine`/`#explore`/`#farm` take no coords
and a legal `#goto` can still PATH THROUGH the zone (baritone cannot be told
to route around it). So the log-tail position parser doubles as watchdog:
parsed position inside the padded box → immediately `msg #stop`, then
`msg #goto <camp waypoint>`, mark task `aborted:nogo` in `/status`, log loud.
Watchdog is the backstop; the gate is the front door. Drivers should also
prefer targets whose straight line to the bot doesn't cross the box.

## Upstream status 2026-09-01

Research pass (gh CLI, no installs/launches) into the two blockers hit trying
to bring PATH 1 up on HMC 2.10.0 / MC 1.21.11: (1) `-lwjgl` render patch hangs
forever pre-title-screen after spamming "Found unknown and unsupported uniform
in minecraft:blur/0" through "blur/5"; (2) hmc-specifics' JLine console
misbehaves when stdio is a plain pipe (no TTY), as the wrapper needs.

### Blocker 1 — `-lwjgl` render hang on blur uniforms

Root cause, near-certain: the exact string "Found unknown and unsupported
uniform" is **vanilla Mojang code**, not a headlessmc string — confirmed by
grepping public 1.21.11 decompile mirrors, it lives in
`com.mojang.blaze3d.opengl.GlProgram`. On a real GPU this line is a harmless,
non-fatal WARN. The hang is a HeadlessMc-side consequence: `-lwjgl` works by
bytecode-redirecting LWJGL/GL calls to fake return values instead of talking
to a real GPU (`headlessmc-lwjgl/.../redirections/LwjglRedirections.java`),
and that emulation layer is incomplete for the newer RenderPipeline/GPU-device
abstraction Mojang shipped around 1.21.9-1.21.11 and is still shipping today
(Mojang has since moved to calendar version numbers — 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.2 all
come chronologically *after* 1.21.11 in this same codebase's version list).

Evidence the maintainers are actively chasing this exact surface, release by
release:
- **2.9.0** (2026-04-04): [PR #407](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/407)
  "fix(1.21.11): Fix crash" — fixed `MemoryUtil;memSlice`, which had literally
  been stubbed to always `return null` ("TODO... null is fairly safe rn"),
  causing the 1.21.11 boot NPE in
  [issue #388](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/388).
  Sibling [PR #406](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/406) fixed
  the same-shaped 1.21.10 crash,
  [issue #389](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/389).
- **2.10.0** (2026-07-13): [PR #426](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/pull/426)
  "fix(26.2): Fixed lwjgl headless launching for 26.2" — fixed `DeviceLimits`/
  `GPUDevices` emulation gaps for the version right after 1.21.11.
- 1.21.11's own build support was gated on
  [headlesshq/mc-runtime-test#116](https://github.com/headlesshq/mc-runtime-test/issues/116)
  (unimined tooling), closed 2026-04-04 — separate from the runtime bugs above.
- No release newer than 2.10.0 exists; commits on `main` since the 2.10.0 tag
  are chore-only (logo, CI) — nothing queued that would fix this.
- Exhaustive search (issues/PRs/commits/discussions/code-search, org-wide) for
  "blur" or "uniform" turns up **nothing** else — the only unrelated hit is
  `hmc.lwjgl.uniformoffsetalignment` (`GL_UNIFORM_BUFFER_OFFSET_ALIGNMENT`,
  a buffer-alignment constant, not the blur pipeline's uniform names). **This
  exact hang is unreported upstream as of 2.10.0 / today.**
- No LwjglProperties flag exists to selectively skip RenderPipeline/uniform
  validation while staying in `-lwjgl` mode. `hmc.lwjgl.ignore.classes`
  exists but excluding a class from redirection while headless just crashes
  it against a real GL call with no context — not a usable escape hatch.

**Workaround that should fix it today: stop using `-lwjgl`.** HeadlessMc's
own README says outright: "You can also achieve headless mode without
patching lwjgl by running headlessmc with a virtual framebuffer like Xvfb."
More to the point for us: BariBrute's host is a normal Windows desktop with a
real GPU and display, not a headless VM — there is no rendering gap to paper
over in the first place. Launching fabric 1.21.11 *without* `-lwjgl` uses
real, unpatched LWJGL against the real GPU driver, so the blur-uniform WARN
gets handled exactly as on any normal player client (logged once, harmless,
game keeps rendering) because it never touches headlessmc's incomplete
redirection layer at all.
- hmc-specifics' console (`msg`, `connect`, `gui`, `click`) is confirmed to
  work identically with or without `-lwjgl` — see maintainer replies in
  [issue #230](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/230) and
  [issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390). Baritone
  chat-command control (part 3 of this doc) is unaffected by dropping the
  flag.
- Trade-off: a real (small, minimizable) game window per bot instance, and a
  sliver of real GPU/VRAM per client instead of zero. JVM heap budget in part
  6 is unaffected (that's CPU RAM, not GPU).
- If this stack ever moves to a true headless Linux box with no GPU at all,
  the Linux-native equivalent is Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe (software GL) in front
  of an un-patched launch — a working docker recipe is in
  [issue #249](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/249) (needs
  the `x11-xserver-utils` package per maintainer 3arthqu4ke, plus
  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`). Not directly usable on bare Windows (no X11);
  would need WSL2. Untested by this pass — field-verify separately if needed.
- If dropping `-lwjgl` is rejected and true headless is a hard requirement:
  this bucket is "fixable soon, not now" — file a new upstream issue with the
  exact blur/uniform log lines + HMC 2.10.0 + MC 1.21.11 fabric. The
  maintainers (okafke, 3arthqu4ke) have a strong track record on this exact
  bug family — #388/#389 to merged fixes #406/#407 the same day.

### Blocker 2 — JLine console over a plain pipe (no TTY)

Confirmed root cause + confirmed fix, from
[issue #390](https://github.com/headlesshq/headlessmc/issues/390)
"Hmc-Specifics messes up command line" (non-interactive-shaped terminal,
reporter on a Raspberry Pi): the maintainer's own prescribed and
reporter-confirmed fix is setting **`hmc.jline.enabled=false`** in
`HeadlessMC/config.properties` (also documented in the README's Termux
section — "Disable JLine, as we could not get it to work on Termux for now").

Caveat from that same thread: the reporter *also* had the deprecated
`-commands` runtime flag active alongside hmc-specifics, which caused a
separate "every second command works" flakiness. Maintainer's explicit
guidance: never combine `-commands` with hmc-specifics — hmc-specifics alone
is the console surface. PATH 1 in this doc already avoids `-commands` — stay
that way.

`headlessmc-jline/.../JLineProperties.java` exposes finer-grained flags no
one in the tracker has field-tested for this exact scenario but which read as
a more surgical fix than fully disabling JLine:
- `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` — auto-fall-back to JLine's
  dumb-terminal mode only when no real console/TTY is detected (exactly our
  "wrapper pipes stdio" case), keeping normal JLine behavior everywhere else.
- `hmc.jline.dumb=true` — force dumb mode unconditionally, the blunter
  version of the above.

No mention anywhere in the org (issues, discussions, code) of node-pty or
ConPTY wrapping — that is **not** a known/documented HMC pattern. The
maintainer-endorsed route is purely the config-property route above; no
reason to stand up a pty shim.

**Recommended order:** try `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first
(least invasive); fall back to `hmc.jline.enabled=false` (the confirmed fix
from #390) if commands still misbehave over the wrapper's plain pipe.

### Alternatives sanity check

- **Automatone** ([Ladysnake/Automatone](https://github.com/Ladysnake/Automatone),
  active, last updated 2026-07-10) — confirmed dead end for this stack, as
  suspected. It's a **server-side Fabric mod**: you attach Baritone pathing to
  any entity via a Java `EntityComponentFactory` registered server-side
  (`BaritoneAPI.getProvider().getBaritone(entity)`), driven entirely by
  in-process Java API calls. There is no protocol-level or console/chat
  control surface at all — mineflayer (an external protocol client) has
  nothing to hook into. Not usable, full stop.
- No other maintained "real headless Java client + baritone" project exists
  for 1.21.x besides HeadlessMc + hmc-specifics + official Baritone (PATH 1,
  already chosen). Official Baritone itself is healthy and current:
  [cabaletta/baritone releases](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone/releases)
  show v1.16.0 (1.21.9/1.21.10), **v1.17.0 (1.21.11 — ours)**, v1.18.0 (26.1),
  v1.19.0 (26.2) — all four pushed 2026-08-31, one release per MC version,
  no drama.
- `Nevarielle/baritone-1.21.11` (community fork) still exists but is now
  redundant — official v1.17.0 covers 1.21.11 directly. Matches this doc's
  existing "obsolete — skip" call, no change needed.

### Verdict

- **Blocker 1 (render hang): fixable now, not via any HMC flag/release, but
  via a launch-config change — drop `-lwjgl`, run BariBrute's client with a
  real (minimized) window on the real GPU.** This sidesteps HeadlessMc's
  incomplete RenderPipeline/uniform emulation, the near-certain cause, which
  is not fixed or even filed upstream for the blur pipeline specifically
  (2.9.0/2.10.0 only fixed the neighboring memSlice-NPE and 26.2 DeviceLimits
  gaps). If a fully invisible process is a hard requirement, this drops to
  "fixable soon" — file upstream and wait; track record is good but nothing
  to point to yet.
- **Blocker 2 (JLine over plain pipe): fixable now** via config property, no
  pty wrapper needed — `hmc.jline.dumb.when.no.console=true` first, else the
  confirmed `hmc.jline.enabled=false` from issue #390. Keep never using
  `-commands` alongside hmc-specifics.
- **Alternatives: no change to PATH 1.** Automatone is confirmed unusable
  (server-side Java-API-only, no external-bot hook); official Baritone
  v1.17.0 for 1.21.11 remains current and healthy.

### Exact next actions

3. Do not add `-commands` anywhere — hmc-specifics alone is the console

4. If `-lwjgl` is ever required again (e.g. a true headless Linux box with no
